ask: Publish a versioned fact freeze separating UN civilian data, party claims and independent reporting.
mechanism: Reduce decision errors caused by conflation of an announced truce with a signed one.
gate: Source date, rights review, citations and public-only scope.
measure: Every material claim has a source, category and last-checked date.
stop: Retract or qualify disputed facts; do not release sensitive locations.
cost: Low desk-research cost; staff time variable.

ask: Draft at least three alternative explanations for negotiation deadlock and an observable refutation for each.
mechanism: Make policy discussions robust against mono-causal assumptions.
gate: Independent review, attribution and political neutrality.
measure: Disconfirming evidence and confidence revisions publicly tracked.

owner: Manufacturers, distributors and export regulators within authority
ask: Conduct voluntary public high-priority-component provenance review and clarify third-country diversion mechanisms.
mechanism: Narrow lawful investigative leads and reduce false allegations.
gate: Legal counsel, protected commercial data safeguards and due process.
measure: Named model/shipper/recipient links corroborated or corrected.
stop: Suspend outreach when identity or component linkage is unverified.

ask: Publish public civilian-impact and ceasefire-status baselines with transparent coverage gaps.
mechanism: Support the evaluation of reciprocal civilian-protection proposals.
gate: No release of protected individuals or vulnerable system detail.
measure: Updated aggregate data and explicitly dated confidence classifications.

owner: State Department, authorized negotiators and agreed neutral facilitators
ask: Evaluate written sectoral energy/humanitarian truce terms before declaring success.
mechanism: Verify mutual consent, scope and independent adjudication.
gate: Negotiating-party consent and legal safeguards; CIA does not set policy.
measure: Mutually acknowledged agreement, observer coverage and verified compliance.
stop: Do not announce implementation without written terms and operational monitoring.

owner: U.S./Canadian regulatory authorities and corporate compliance teams
ask: Review documented sanctions-evasion networks while explicitly protecting lawful defense and humanitarian trade.
mechanism: Discourage knowing illicit procurement without collective suspicion.
gate: National export law, standards of proof and rights review.
measure: Verified cases resolved with recorded rebuttals and legal outcomes.
stop: Review if unintended civilian impacts outweigh objective gains.

owner: Governments, UN-mandated or consent-based observers and local stakeholders
ask: Design rights-respecting ceasefire verification, safeguards and violation appeals.
mechanism: Reduce the credible-commitment gap through reciprocal observable compliance.
gate: Independent mandates, lawful authority, negotiated access and non-recognition of unlawful annexation.
measure: Aggregate verified incidents, time to adjudication, appeals outcomes and civilian access.
stop: Suspend unsafe disclosures and revert to minimum humanitarian protection.

owner: Ukraine-led reconstruction authorities, multilateral lenders and communities
ask: Develop transparent rights-centered recovery and non-recurrence accountability indicators.
mechanism: Make peace materially credible while retaining sovereignty and humanitarian standards.
gate: Ukrainian agency, audited governance and international law.
measure: Civilian infrastructure reliability, displacement outcomes, and verified non-recurrence.
stop: Correct corruption or discriminatory access through independent review.
